evidence: Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml has [weights] functional = 0.6, polish = 0.2, visual = 0.2, gates render/constraints = 0.0 and [floors] functional = 0.05, byte-for-byte the template values, and task score.py is identical to the template score.py (diff clean). This matches the skill ('functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2 - behind two zero-weight gates and a functional floor') and the internal workbook note for row 44 ('Functionality has 60 pecent'). Maximum contribution of the non-functional dimensions is 0.40 against 0.60 for functionality, and none of it is paid when functional <= 0.05. No weight key sits in any [judge] block; every dimension uses aggregation = weighted_mean; gates carry no reward mass. Criterion weights (parsed with tomllib): functional has 42 binary criteria totalling 58.5 = 15 at 1.0, 21 at 1.5, 6 at 2.0, a narrow 1:2 spread, so no single criterion exceeds 3.4% of the dimension (2.05% of the reward). The 2.0 tier is cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic, cw_same_line_carets, cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo, cw_last_good_recovery, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work and cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state: each is a multi-step compound behaviour named in the brief ('paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it', 'without losing a draft when another tab saves first') and each proves several facts with a control or an undo/redo round trip. The 1.0 tier holds single-fact or prerequisite outcomes (cw_basic_run_output, cw_html_preview, cw_console_levels_in_order, cw_custom_typing_and_line_join, cw_mouse_selection, cw_html_semantic_coloring, cw_format_error_keeps_draft). Mass by product area: editing 16.0 (27.4%), find/replace 5.0 (8.5%), syntax colouring 2.5 (4.3%), formatting 4.5 (7.7%), run/preview/isolation 19.5 (33.3%), persistence/revisions/live update 11.0 (18.8%). The only appearance-flavoured functional criteria are the two colouring ones (2.5 of 58.5); they require a working tokenizer with five distinct categories, which is behaviour, and they are not weighted above the runtime or persistence groups. Polish has 6 binary criteria at 1.0 each and visual has 3 likert criteria at 1.0 each, equal weights as in the template, so pure appearance is capped at 0.20 of the reward and behaviour-of-controls at another 0.20. Negative criteria at 1.5-2.0 (cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, cw_dynamic_code_refused, cw_preview_isolation, cw_stale_save_refused) each demand a positive working control inside the same criterion, so a dead feature cannot collect their weight by doing nothing. Limits of this verdict: this is a source reading of the weights on the frozen bytes. The scripted golden results in raw-evidence-index.json (hashes verified) show the reference app satisfies the 42 Functional and 6 Polish checks but say nothing about weighting; the hosted judge run is on an earlier candidate with 41 functional criteria and is not a measurement of these bytes. No runtime measurement is required to decide this row. Observation, not a defect: cw_basic_run_output is at the lowest weight although Run is the most basic outcome; it is a prerequisite for roughly twenty other functional criteria, so a Run-less app loses far more than 1.0 and the ordering stays honest.
